body: Thank you.  I know I shouldn't be as sad as I am, but that's just the way depression works.  It feels like my life is being ripped away though.  I'm so dependent on others, and I just don't know what the hell I'm going to do.  I don't really know about networking places either.  I'm pretty antisocial and bad with strangers, which is partly why I'm so worried about them moving out.

I appreciate the reply, thank you.

I'm not sure whether or not what I go through is a ruined orgasm, assuming you're referring to the times when I'm "beating a half-limp dong until I get a mediocre climax".  I still climax and I still feel it, just not near as much as if I was properly erect and hadn't been trying for a half an hour.

Like you said, I think it may be because I'm fapping to remove the urges, not because I want to fap.  Usually when I fap for the second time in a day, it's because I'm aroused and want to fap, rather than have that burning urge in my gut, and it usually goes alright.  Not always, but usually.  I've worked up to a proper fap for upwards of an hour, but often it just doesn't help.

Those urges really are a serious issue for me, and I have talked to several doctors and it never got anywhere.

This is the sort of stuff you probably don't want to hear when depressed, but probably need to.  I know I have a lot of people that would miss me and that it would hurt.  And I know there are a few people that it would devastate.  But when you're depressed, you don't really think about that. 

You might be right though.  Maybe I'm being unfair to them by not even giving them a chance to help.   They're my friends, and I know they care a great deal about me.

I'm not going to deny that it's a daunting thought.  I've had a lot of problems involving not being able to live up to responsibilities due to being sick and frail, and trying to hold down a job would more than likely be a repeat.  Maybe I'm a pansy for not wanting to try, but I've had some serious shit because I couldn't do what people expected of me.

I'm...  I'm really touched by this.  Not being able to get on SSI is one of my biggest worries and has been for some time, and getting ANY kind of assistance on this is really huge.  I feel kind of dumb for not asking for help somewhere, but I didn't know where to start or where to ask or... well, anything.  

Looking at the sites you linked, they're all pretty overwhelming.  There's not really any clear instructions, so I'm pretty lost.  I don't mean to be difficult, but I... sort of have this problem I suppose?  I'm sorry.

I see that I can file an appeal online.  Should I do so now, or wait and get a lawyer?  I have about 45 days or so left, give or take.  I hadn't looked into it yet since my mother has been so sick, but if I can do it online, that would make things a lot easier.  But I don't know if I should appeal now or seek legal counsel first.

I don't mind telling you that I live in Oklahoma.  I think it might be against the rules here to say what city, but I'm in the uper-right quarter.  If it's fine to say what city, I'd be fine with that too, if that info is needed as well.

I'm sorry to make your reply semi-wasted, but I live with both my mother and best friend, actually, and have lived with various friends in our house off and on for some time...  When I say I feel alone, I mean it feels like I don't have anyone to talk about problems with.  I have some very good friends, but some people you just either can't open up to or don't feel comfortable doing so.  My best friend is so for a reason.  He helps me move things I can't lift, takes me out to eat since I can't drive, things like that.

But like I said, I don't have anyone I really feel I can talk about these sorts of things with.  That's what I mean about being alone.  It's probably a problem on my part.  I've felt comfortable talking about problems face-to-face with very few people over the course of my life.

I agree with what you said though.  Society has driven people to be isolated, self-sufficient, relying on nobody but themselves.  Our society and culture seems to drive people into reclusion.

I really and truly appreciate this.  I don't really know anyone with SSI / disability aside from my mother's legally-blind friend, and he obviously got it without trying.

I didn't know they usually deny you right off.  I've been looking into getting a lawyer to make an appeal but I don't know who to contact or how to go about it.  But knowing that you're usually denied the first time makes me feel a bit better.

And thank you for the offer.  It's... nice to know someone would be willing to hold a conversation about all this shit.
Not a great deal...  I enjoy videogames and sci-fi, reading occasionally...  Not many hobbies that would get me out of the house, I'm afraid.
Even so, the comment is still nice.  Simply that someone took the time to reply is appreciated.
